Apply that same relation here. Each gift box needs 9 units of ribbon, 4 of cards, and 8 of beads; in stock you have 75 units of ribbon, 47 of cards, and 75 of beads. Which resource runs out first (caps the count), and how many gift boxes do you get? (The resource you have least of by raw amount is a distractor.)
Reason it through step by step before answering.

reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Compute the supported count for each: ribbon = 75/9 = 8; cards = 47/4 = 11; beads = 75/8 = 9 gift boxes.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Name the distractor: by raw amount the scarcest is cards (47 units), which the surface reading would wrongly pick.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: By the intended relation the minimum supported count is 8, at ribbon, even though its raw stock (75) is not the smallest.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

reasoning_trace.text: Check: 8 gift boxes consume 72 of ribbon (<= 75), 32 of cards (<= 47), 64 of beads (<= 75); one more would need 81 of ribbon, exceeding 75. Mapping confirmed.
reasoning_trace.label: valid

final_answer: Ribbon runs out first; you can complete 8 gift boxes.

verification.details: Binding constraint recomputed: min(stock/need) = 8 at ribbon; the raw-scarcest resource cards is correctly rejected as a distractor.
